title: Procurement and vendor management
description: Review the purchase of software, services and data from third parties: need, selection, due diligence, contract and exit.
expertises: Contract terms, renewals and exit plans
questions: What need does the purchase answer, and which alternatives were compared?
What data, access and dependency does the vendor get, and how was its security checked?
How do we leave this vendor, and what does it cost?

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1, Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations
NCSC, Principles of supply chain security
ENISA, Good Practices for Supply Chain Cybersecurity (2023)

specialists.title: Sourcing lead
specialists.focus: Check that the need is written down, that more than one option was compared on the same criteria and that the total cost covers the whole term.
checks: The comparison uses the same weighted criteria for every vendor, fixed before the offers were read.
Total cost covers licences, implementation, support, usage tiers and price increases over the contract term.
The internal owner and the budget line are named before the order is signed.

specialists.title: Third-party risk analyst
specialists.focus: Classify the vendor by the data and access it receives and run the due diligence that matches: security questionnaire, certifications, subprocessors and financial health.
checks: The vendor's criticality is recorded with the reason: data handled, access granted, service dependency.
A certification report is read for its scope and period, not only its logo, and its exceptions are noted.
Subprocessors and data locations are listed and compared with what the company promised its own customers.

specialists.title: Contract terms specialist
specialists.focus: Compare the vendor contract with the company's requirements: service levels, data processing, audit rights, liability, renewal and notice periods.
checks: A data processing agreement is signed when the vendor processes personal data on the company's behalf.
Automatic renewal dates and notice periods are entered in a calendar with an owner.
Service levels have remedies, and the measurement method is defined in the contract.

specialists.title: Exit and continuity planner
specialists.focus: Write how the company would leave the vendor: data export format, transition period, replacement options and the cost and time to switch.
checks: The contract gives a data export in a documented format and a transition period after termination.
The exit plan names an alternative vendor or an in-house fallback and the time to switch.
Critical vendors have a test of the export, not only a clause.

evidence: Written need, options compared and the scoring grid used.
Vendor security questionnaire, certification reports and subprocessor list, with dates.
Draft contract, data processing agreement, service levels and renewal terms.
Exit plan with data export format, transition period and alternatives.
challenge: Was the vendor chosen before the comparison started, and does the grid reflect that?
What would happen to our customers if this vendor stopped service tomorrow?
Does the vendor get more data or access than the need requires?
Which renewal or price increase will surprise the budget owner next year?
decision_criteria: Proceed when the need, comparison, due diligence and contract terms are documented and the owner signs off.
Revise when the vendor's access or data exceeds the need, or the contract lacks a data processing agreement where one is required.
Escalate when a critical vendor has no tested exit or a due diligence finding stays open, to the risk owner who can accept it.
Record the renewal date, notice period and the review date for the vendor's risk rating.
